title: When the Reference Has a Hole
scenario: It is 6:18 AM. The forecast arrived - for two of the three hubs. WAUE joined the desk last month and the forecast model does not produce a number for it yet. A reference with a hole raises ownership and behavior questions the easy tier never had to ask.
input:
Forecast per hub, published nightly by the desk's forecast model:
ERCOT: 188
SPP: 100
WAUE: (not produced - hub not yet in the model)

Governance on file: the internal model is the authoritative forecast. The model is owned by the Forecast Model Owner; adding a hub to it is that owner's change to make, on their release schedule.
instructions: Note which hubs have references and which do not.

questions.prompt: Why is WAUE missing from the forecast?

options.text: The file was truncated in transit
The model does not know the hub yet - a coverage gap, not a delivery failure
WAUE prices are too small to forecast

questions.explain: The input says it directly: hub not yet in the model. Diagnosing WHY a value is missing decides what to do about it - a coverage gap and a broken delivery have different fixes.

questions.prompt: What should Variance Check do about WAUE this morning?

options.text: Use ERCOT's forecast as a stand-in - hubs are similar enough
Use zero as the forecast so the math still runs
Exclude WAUE from forecast comparison - compute nothing you cannot defend

questions.explain: A borrowed or zero forecast produces a delta that LOOKS real and is fiction. The honest behavior is exclusion, with the gap visible.

questions.prompt: Whose job is it to close the gap?

options.text: The Forecast Model Owner - source-of-truth changes belong to the source owner
The morning workflow - it should synthesize a forecast
Nobody - the gap resolves itself over time

questions.explain: The governance line names the owner and the change path. Consumers of a reference do not patch the reference; they route the request to its owner.

questions.prompt: Can WAUE still be risk-classified this morning?

options.text: No - one missing reference disqualifies a hub from everything
Yes - day-over-day classification needs only the prior-day baseline, which exists
Only if the Desk Manager approves an exception

questions.explain: Different steps have different data requirements. The threshold policy classifies on the day-over-day move, and WAUE has a prior-day value - the forecast gap does not infect that computation.

artifactOnPass.gap: WAUE not produced (hub not yet in model)
artifactOnPass.consumerBehavior: variance excludes WAUE from forecast comparison

copilotPrompt: Assess a reference gap: diagnose why the value is missing, decide the consumer's honest behavior, name who owns closing the gap, and identify what remains computable despite it.
successMessage: Gap assessed. The workflow knows what to skip, what still works, and whose queue the fix belongs in.

intro.heading: Before you judge: references fail partially

sections.title: Diagnose before deciding
sections.body: A missing value has many possible causes - truncation, renames, coverage gaps - and each has a different correct response. The first move is always: why is it missing?

sections.title: Consumers do not patch sources
sections.body: The tempting fix (invent a WAUE forecast) quietly makes the workflow the author of reference data it does not own. Gaps route to the source owner; consumers behave honestly in the meantime.

sections.title: Partial failure is not total failure
sections.body: The gap breaks one comparison for one hub. Everything else - two full variance rows, three risk classifications - still works. Scoping the blast radius precisely is the skill.

takeaway.heading: Reference gap assessed
points: You diagnosed the gap (coverage, not breakage) before choosing a response - the diagnosis IS the decision.
You kept the workflow honest: exclusion over fabrication, with the gap visible downstream.
You routed the fix to the source owner instead of patching someone else's data.
You scoped the blast radius: one comparison lost, day-over-day classification intact.
The workflow can now operate correctly against a reference that is only partially there.
